title: What is known about 1RB1RD_1LC0LC_1RD1LB_1RF0RE_0RA1RE_---1RB
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1RD_1LC0LC_1RD1LB_1RF0RE_0RA1RE_---1RB.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. At each visit of the left end the tape is a block of 011111 words that grows, then a region transformed by a fixed map: a chaotic near zone, a reservoir of runs of five 1s, and a far zone that is reached by rare sweeps crossing the whole reservoir (16 times in 300,000 sweeps). Two events so far (after sweeps 33 and 8,347) each turned the block into a new reservoir; the present one, 16,600 cells, should last about 22400 sweeps. A halt needs two 0s in a row, which only the far end offers.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 58,204 cells have been visited and 41,692 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: The sweep map ignores the block; two events
claims.text: At each visit of the left end in state B the tape is B>0 111 (011111)^n R. With the block cut to 10 words at every visit, R agrees with the true run at all of the first 9,000 visits. Events after visits 33 (R from 35 to 92 cells) and 8,347 (95 to 16,724 cells).

claims.title: No halt in 4·10<sup>6</sup> sweeps after the second event
claims.text: From visit 8,400 the shortened run makes 4·10<sup>6</sup> visits (about 3·10<sup>13</sup> steps of the true run) without a halt or an event.

claims.title: Rare sweeps cross the whole reservoir
claims.text: In the 300,000 visits after 8,400, sixteen sweeps go through the reservoir to the far zone: at visits 8406, 8445, 8454, 8736, 9142, 9621, 10678, 10686, 10902, 16800, 27549, 57888, 158742, 170205, 268341 and 272566.

claims.title: No halt in the first 3.01×10<sup>14</sup> steps (region-memo accelerator)
claims.text: The region-memo accelerator tools/py/bbtools/regaccel.py ran the mirrored table (so that the counter is at the left end), with blocks of 6 cells, from blank tape for 600 seconds and reached step 3.01×1014 without a halt. It keeps the tape run-length coded and, for each stretch of tape from the left end, a macro (the run until the head first leaves that stretch) computed by a symbolic run of the machine with the long runs as variables; a macro is used only when the linear inequalities its symbolic run assumed hold, otherwise the stretch is run again by the same recursion. So the run is exact, step count included. Check: 3000 configurations of this run (every time the head faced blank tape on the right, up to 2×109 steps) agree cell for cell with a direct run (tools/py/regcheck.py). This is a bounded run and says nothing about later steps.

claims.title: Next event about 2<sup>2400</sup> sweeps away
claims.text: The near zone eats about 7 cells of reservoir per doubling of the number of sweeps; the reservoir has about 16,600 cells.

claims.title: A scaled-down version halts
claims.text: With the block cut to 2 words at every visit from the start, the run halts after 24,517 visits; with 3, 4 or 5 words there is no halt in 2·10<sup>7</sup> visits.

claims.title: Growth shape: fixed/sqrt
claims.text: The head sweeps across the whole tape and adds a word per sweep at the left end, so the tape grows like the square root of the step count.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The laws of the near and far zones are not known, and neither is what happens when they meet.

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same table as 1RB0RB_1LC1RA_1LF0LD_0LE1LD_1LA1LC_---1LA up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. A block of repeated words grows at every sweep; behind it a scrambled counter nibbles at a long reservoir, and once in a long while a sweep runs through the whole reservoir and disturbs the far end. This page runs the real machine in your browser and explains the pieces.

facts.text: The region behind the block since the second event (sweep 8,347): mostly a reservoir of runs of five 1s.
Sweeps that ran through the whole reservoir in 300,000 sweeps, at ever longer intervals.
Estimated wait for the next event.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.

sections.heading: A growing block and a reservoir with two busy ends
html: Look at the tape each time the head reaches the left end. First comes a block of copies of the word 011111, one more than last time. Then a region made of runs of 1s of odd length separated by single 0s: a few dozen busy cells with runs of all sorts of lengths, then a very long stretch of runs of exactly five 1s (the reservoir), and at the far end a second, smaller irregular zone.

<svg viewBox="0 0 580 70" role="img" aria-label="The tape: a growing uniform block, an active counter region, a reservoir it eats, and an old tail at the far end" style="width:100%;max-width:620px;height:auto"><g font-family="var(--body)" font-size="11" fill="var(--fg2)"><text x="10" y="14">← grows one word a sweep</text><text x="14" y="60">growing block</text><text x="184" y="60">busy counter</text><text x="274" y="60">reservoir</text><text x="484" y="60">old tail</text></g><rect x="10" y="20" width="170" height="22" fill="var(--ink)" stroke="var(--line-strong)"/><rect x="180" y="20" width="90" height="22" fill="var(--heur-bg)" stroke="var(--line-strong)"/><rect x="270" y="20" width="210" height="22" fill="var(--accent-soft)" stroke="var(--line-strong)"/><rect x="480" y="20" width="90" height="22" fill="var(--sunk)" stroke="var(--line-strong)"/></svg>
As in its sister machines, crossing the block changes nothing: the machine applies one fixed rule to the region behind the block, sweep after sweep.

sections.heading: Two counters, one at each end
html: The near zone behaves like a scrambled odometer: it changes at almost every sweep and advances into the reservoir by about 7 cells each time the number of sweeps doubles.

What is special here is the far zone. Usually a sweep turns around in the near zone. But now and then one keeps going, runs through thousands of five-runs, and changes the far zone before coming back. In the 300,000 sweeps after the last event this happened 16 times, at sweeps 8406, 8445, 8454, 8736, 9142, 9621, 10678, 10686, 10902, 16800, 27549, 57888, 158742, 170205, 268341 and 272566: more and more rarely, like a second, much slower counter.

When the near zone has eaten the whole reservoir there is an event: the block becomes a new reservoir and a new block starts. That happened after sweeps 33 and 8,347. The present reservoir should last about 22400 sweeps.

sections.heading: A coin toss, repeated at ever longer intervals
html: Between two events nothing can go wrong: the machine sweeps, the block grows, the counter eats a little more reservoir. Everything is decided in the few sweeps in which the counter touches the far end of the tape. Each such contact either stops the machine or turns the block into the next reservoir, which is as long as the block had become, so the next contact is exponentially further away than the last one, and the one after that exponentially further again.

<svg viewBox="0 0 580 96" role="img" aria-label="Epochs: each reservoir is as long as the block was at the previous event, so each epoch is exponentially longer than the one before" style="width:100%;max-width:620px;height:auto"><g font-family="var(--body)" font-size="11" fill="var(--fg2)"><text x="10" y="14">epoch k: reservoir of L cells</text><text x="10" y="58">epoch k+1: reservoir of about 2^(L/c) cells</text><text x="300" y="36">eaten in about 2^(L/c) sweeps</text></g><rect x="10" y="20" width="60" height="18" fill="var(--accent-soft)" stroke="var(--line-strong)"/><rect x="70" y="20" width="14" height="18" fill="var(--sunk)" stroke="var(--line-strong)"/><rect x="10" y="64" width="520" height="18" fill="var(--accent-soft)" stroke="var(--line-strong)"/><rect x="530" y="64" width="14" height="18" fill="var(--sunk)" stroke="var(--line-strong)"/><circle cx="84" cy="29" r="4" fill="var(--head)"/><circle cx="544" cy="73" r="4" fill="var(--head)"/></svg>

Machines like this are called cryptids in the Busy Beaver community: their fate hangs on an unbounded sequence of yes/no questions about a pseudo-random process, and no known method answers all of them at once.

The machine halts only if state D finds two 0s in a row; inside the tape every 0 stands alone, so this can only happen where the tape ends. A scaled-down version of the machine (block kept at two words) does halt, after 24,517 sweeps; versions with three to five words did not within 20 million sweeps. The real machine's next chance comes at the next event.

sections.heading: What was checked, and how
html:
• A version of the machine that cuts the block back to 10 words at every sweep sees exactly the same region as the real machine at each of the first 9,000 sweeps.
  • That version runs 4 million sweeps past the second event (3·1013 real steps) without a halt.
  • Not known: the exact rule of either zone.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machine below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in the other, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

family: two chaotic counters around a reservoir of five-runs (cryptid-like)
summary: A block of 011111 words grows at the left; behind it a chaotic near zone eats a reservoir of runs of five 1s (about 7 cells per doubling of sweeps) while rare sweeps cross the reservoir and change a far zone; events after sweeps 33 and 8,347, the next about 2^2400 sweeps away.
